page: OVHcloud r3-256-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server built for high memory density and multi-core computational tasks. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform running at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 1 thread per core without hyperthreading, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 256.0 GB RAM, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. Storage is handled by a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and networking provides a baseline throughput of 8 Gbps. The server operates under KVM virtualization without attached GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive memory and multi-core capabilities. The PassMark memory test registers in the top 10% tier at 3012.0, corroborated by uncached large-block read speeds of 274.2 GB/sec and write speeds of 110.76 GB/sec. Multi-threaded computational results also rank within the top 25%, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 98363.28, a Geekbench multi-core score of 18507.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 63302.15. Data operations show robust capacity, with Redis SET operations achieving 73.99 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 31814.61.

Single-threaded workloads and CPU-bound compression tasks deliver moderate results. Single-core tests place within the middle 50% tier, showing 1893.0 on Geekbench single-core, 28.98 GB/sec on gzip compression, and 13.31 GB/sec on single-threaded bzip3 decompression. The CPU lacks AVX-512 extensions and advanced matrix instructions, limiting dense vector acceleration for larger machine learning models. Additionally, the 50 GB local NVMe disk provides minimal space relative to the system's 256 GB RAM, serving primarily as a boot volume rather than persistent primary storage.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r3-256-flex provides balanced value by pairing dedicated AMD EPYC physical execution cores with a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. This makes it an effective profile for in-memory caching layers, Redis clusters, intermediate ETL processing, large software build pipelines, and transactional database nodes where main memory bandwidth and predictable multi-core scaling take precedence over local drive volume.

Configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, it features 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per-core allocation. Storage includes a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, backed by an 8 Gbps network interface and KVM virtualization without GPU support. Performance benchmarks position the r3-256-flex in the top tiers for memory bandwidth, multi-core throughput, and database execution, scoring 3012.0 in PassMark memory tests and 73.99 million Redis SET operations per second. With dedicated core execution and high RAM density, the instance is well suited for in-memory data stores, distributed caching, relational databases, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines.
